entries.title: Clean profile identity header
entries.detail: Removed the pill button highlight and circular cutout around the account status on your profile. The handle and membership status are rendered as clean, plain typography without intrusive button containers.

entries.title: Dedicated manga specifications and progress
entries.detail: Manga entries in the activity feed and detail specs now correctly display chapters and volumes rather than episodes and runtimes. Manga details distinguish serialization publishers and reading progress without anime-specific terms.

entries.title: Enhanced provider and profile backgrounds
entries.detail: Refined atmospheric backdrop gradients and higher quality art for the demo provider, ensuring rich contrast and seamless edge blending.

entries.title: Dashboard avatar and title polish
entries.detail: The dashboard top bar employs consistent rounded squircle avatars instead of circular cutouts, keeping your name and title crisp and uncluttered.

entries.title: Favourites open the in-app anime info
entries.detail: Tapping a pinned anime or manga on a profile's Home tab opens the same detail sheet the activity feed uses - synopsis, community scores, rankings, genres, specs and an AniList link - instead of handing the tap to the browser. A favourite is a show someone chose to show off, so it should answer with everything the app already knows how to render. Characters, staff and studios have no media sheet, so they keep the external link.

entries.title: Your name on the dashboard opens your profile
entries.detail: The viewer's handle in the dashboard's top bar is now a second way into the profile, next to the avatar. A name is what a person reads and taps, so the whole identity block answers to it - tapping your name opens your AniList profile just as the avatar always has.

entries.title: Widgets stop naming shows they are not showing
entries.detail: A tile with no entry to name now hides its title instead of showing the app name as if it were the show's title, so a missed-sequels tile that is empty no longer claims a show nobody is missing. The featured tile's "Sequel to …" line does the same when a recommendation has no parent, rather than rendering as a sentence with its subject missing.

entries.title: The activity tile shows your face
entries.detail: The activity tile drew nothing for a signed-in user because the dashboard has no viewer-activity feed to read from. It now draws your AniList avatar - the face the tile is actually about - and falls back to the demo poster only until the first real load lands.

entries.title: Covers load on one low-priority thread
entries.detail: Every cover fetch shared a single background thread instead of spawning a new one per tile per update, so a system tick plus an app refresh no longer put several downloads in flight at once. The placeholder rectangle is cached by colour and size rather than redrawn on the main thread inside onUpdate, which is what a widget update used to do on every tick.

entries.title: Widgets that name what they count
entries.detail: The home-screen tiles now draw the show they are talking about: the top missed sequel and the first arriving episode each show a cover, its title and what it is, alongside the count and your AniList handle, with the entry's own colour filling the poster frame until the art loads. Covers are fetched off the main thread, and a tile falls back to that colour placeholder whenever there is no artwork or no network, so it never renders blank.

entries.title: A Featured Sequel widget
entries.detail: A fourth tile gives the single most relevant missed sequel room to breathe — a large poster, its title, what it is a sequel to and how many are waiting — so the recommendation is readable before you even open the app.

entries.title: See who liked an activity
entries.detail: Holding the heart on an activity in a profile now opens a small sheet listing everyone who liked it, avatar and name, with the count in the header. The list comes straight from AniList, so it always agrees with the number on the card. A quick tap still toggles your own like exactly as before.

entries.title: Redrawn vectors
entries.detail: Six of the app's hand-drawn icons were rebuilt so they read at a glance: the calendar clock has a real face and hands, the double check is two visible ticks, the franchise branch is a parent-splits-into-two graph, the fullscreen glyph has shafts so it cannot be mistaken for its opposite, the motion bolt gained speed lines, and the surface-tones icon is a layered stack rather than a bisected square.

entries.title: In-app details from the Activity feed and Currently Arriving
entries.detail: Tapping an entry in a profile's Activity tab, or a card in the dashboard's Currently Arriving row, now opens AniSequel's own detail sheet — synopsis, community scores, rankings, genres, specs and an AniList link — instead of sending you straight to the browser. Those rows were a dead end before: only a missed sequel had a detail view, so the screen that carries AniList's description and ratings could not be reached from the feed. The on-demand detail query now fetches the entry's full record, so these rows get the same header, artwork and specs a sequel already had.

entries.title: The detail sheet adapts to what it is showing
entries.detail: An entry with no parent shows an About tab instead of Story & Gaps, and drops the "Sequel to …" card and the add-to-list gesture that would mean nothing for a show already on your list. The AniList link is still there on every entry.

entries.title: Retain Anime Color keeps the colour
entries.detail: Turning it on while an anime detail sheet is open now persists that anime's cover colour as your app accent, so the whole app keeps the anime's hue after the sheet closes and across restarts — no more watching it fade back to your old theme. Switching it off, or picking a palette, a hue, or Reset appearance, takes back control. This was a stored but never-applied setting; it now does what its label promised.

entries.title: Theme tab, rebuilt around Material 3 Expressive
entries.detail: Settings > Theme leads with a live preview hero washed in the scheme's own colours, then answers three questions in order: how the app looks (appearance mode, then how dark the background is), where the colour comes from (accent palettes and hues, then the anime cover), and how the app moves. Every section and every motion style carries its own vector icon, palettes are chosen from gradient swatches, custom hues are round chips with adaptive check marks, and the anime section shows which cover colour is live and whether it is retained or temporary. Sections read in one scroll, every pick animates with spring physics.

entries.title: GIFs and images in bios and comments
entries.detail: A bare image or GIF link on its own line now shows the picture itself instead of a blue link, and images mixed into a sentence — like a GIF between two words — are embedded in the flow and animate inline.

entries.title: AniList links get a preview card
entries.detail: Pasting an anime, manga, character, staff or studio link now previews it as a card, including links with a www. host or a trailing slash that previously fell through as plain text.

entries.title: Like and comment on activity
entries.detail: The Activity feed's like and reply counts are now buttons. Tap the heart to like or un-like a post, or open a thread to read and post a comment without leaving the app.

entries.title: Theme screen, reorganised
entries.detail: Settings > Theme is now grouped into clear sections — appearance, accent colour, anime colour matching, background and motion. The custom palette and custom hue live in a single accent card, true black and canvas colour share a background card, and reverting an anime colour match back to "Immediately" works again.

entries.title: Theme switching is snappier
entries.detail: Dynamic colour schemes are built once per picked colour instead of on every on-screen change, so changing your accent or theme feels immediate.

entries.title: Planning button no longer double-fires
entries.detail: A long press that you released over the planning target no longer also triggered the quick add at the same time.

entries.title: Refreshing another user's profile lists them correctly
entries.detail: If the profile you are viewing cannot be loaded, Refresh now shows a proper error instead of silently swapping in your own list.

entries.title: Lists are no longer fetched twice
entries.detail: A refresh that lands while the freshness check is already in flight no longer triggers a duplicate fetch of the same lists.

entries.title: Custom lists no longer merge together
entries.detail: Chunked list results are now merged by list name alone, so two custom lists that share a status are kept separate instead of being welded into one.

entries.title: Chunked downloads obey the size cap
entries.detail: Update downloads enforce their size limit inside the read loop, so a server that streams without a Content-Length header can no longer slip an oversized APK past the guard.

entries.title: Year charts sort by the actual year
entries.detail: Release and watch-year charts previously truncated years to two digits, so a 1995 show was ordered as 2095 and a 1999 show merged with a 2019 one. Each year is now counted and ordered correctly, with pre-2000 years shown in full.

entries.title: Home screen widgets show your real numbers
entries.detail: Widgets no longer fall back to sample counts (3, 2, 9 and a demo title) once your account has synced. An empty missed list now hides the previous top title instead of leaving it behind.

entries.title: Adding a sequel no longer keeps it in your missed list
entries.detail: A list fetched while you were adding a title could overwrite the cleared cache and leave that sequel showing as missed until the next refresh. In-flight fetches are now invalidated when you add a title.

entries.title: Refresh recovers instead of hanging
entries.detail: If the viewer profile could not be loaded, tapping Refresh left the dashboard on a spinner with no way back. It now surfaces a retryable error, and returning to the app reliably restarts the freshness check.

entries.title: Recent activity feed keeps what you've loaded
entries.detail: A failed page while scrolling the activity feed no longer wipes the rows already on screen; the footer spinner clears and the next scroll retries.

entries.title: Incomplete downloads no longer masquerade as finished
entries.detail: A failed chunk of a large list now fails the load loudly instead of caching a silently truncated list, and update APKs are cached by version code so a stale file cannot be served for a newer release.

entries.title: More reliable in-app updates
entries.detail: Opening the system installer is now guarded against misconfiguration, and the "Immediately" option for the temporary theme revert works again.

entries.title: Enhanced AniList Markdown & Rich Link Previews
entries.detail: Markdown bios and descriptions now render rich interactive preview cards for AniList links, support animated GIFs with fluid playback, and include robust alignment parsing for centered text and blocks.

entries.title: Animated GIF Support in Markdown
entries.detail: Integrated GIF decoding into Coil so animated image embeds and badges render seamlessly across profile bios and detail views.

entries.title: Tactile bouncy touch feedback across the UI
entries.detail: Restored non-consuming pointer detection in the expressive motion engine so interactive buttons, cards, tabs, and status chips dynamically spring and bounce on press with fluid Material 3 spring physics.

entries.title: Interactive live theme preview card
entries.detail: Added a live interactive preview card in Settings > Theme demonstrating active palettes, custom hues, dark mode, and true black OLED surfaces with interactive sample action buttons.

entries.title: New anime aesthetic palettes
entries.detail: Introduced Midnight Neon (cyberpunk electric cyan and magenta) and Golden Hour (warm amber and copper) curated palettes to the theme selector.

entries.title: Enhanced swatch selection indicators
entries.detail: Palette swatches and custom accent hue pickers now feature tactile bouncy presses, animated spring elevation borders, and smooth selection state indicators.

entries.title: Currently watching & in-list sequels discoverable
entries.detail: The sequel finder can now discover sequels to shows you are currently watching or sequels already in your anime lists. Both options are accessible via new toggles in the filter sheet and remain disabled by default to preserve the classic unwatched gaps feed.

entries.title: New Missed Sequels and Arriving home-screen widgets
entries.detail: Added dedicated home-screen widgets for Missed Sequels and Arriving Soon anime. Placed widgets update with live data from your AniList account and launch directly into relevant dashboard destinations.

entries.title: Enhanced widget performance and data persistence
entries.detail: Widgets now persist live dashboard counts and username details in lightweight local cache, eliminating redundant background fixture queries and synchronizing instantly across updates.

entries.title: Sequel discovery pipeline optimization
entries.detail: Deduplicated sequel candidate allocations during the initial franchise graph exploration, cutting unnecessary object allocations and improving scrolling and filtering responsiveness on accounts with large watch histories.

entries.title: The profile widget can actually be added
entries.detail: The widget's metadata pointed its configuration at a class that is not an Activity, so when the tile was dropped the launcher had nothing to launch - which is a failure reported as the app not being installed. It also never declared an initial layout, so a placed tile had nothing to draw until its first update. Both are now correct, and the widget is registered as its own app widget provider: the forwarding receiver in front of it dropped the update the system sends, so a freshly added tile was never filled in.

entries.title: Tapping the widget opens your activity feed
entries.detail: A tap wrote a request for the profile's Activity screen into the widget's intent and nothing ever read it, so the app opened wherever it was last left. The request is now honoured and the profile opens directly on the Activity tab.

entries.title: A widget that reads at a glance
entries.detail: The tile is redrawn: a rounded surface using the system's own widget radius, an accent bar that follows your device's accent colour, a bold count and one line of context. It previously stacked four centred lines that clipped mid-word once the tile was squashed, and its picker entry shared the same problem. When there is nothing logged yet it says so instead of showing a bare zero.

entries.title: Less work per widget update
entries.detail: Every copy on the home screen now shares one set of views and one tap target, so an update is a single draw and a single round trip to the launcher instead of a full rebuild per instance, and the count behind it is read once per update rather than once per tile.

entries.title: A status you can read without colour
entries.detail: Every status chip now carries its own icon - Airing, Upcoming, Hiatus, Finished and Cancelled - instead of a bare dot. The states were previously distinguished by hue alone, which merges Airing and Upcoming on a grayscale screen and for a colour-blind reader.

entries.title: Anime and manga, told apart
entries.detail: Activity rows are labelled Anime or Manga and the wording follows: a manga row says Chapter 42 rather than Episode 42. Rows with nothing logged yet name their format properly - TV, Movie, OVA - rather than printing "Tv".

entries.title: Spoilers stay open while you scroll
entries.detail: A revealed spoiler used to re-hide itself the moment it scrolled out of view, because the reveal was never saved. It now survives scrolling and rotation, animates open instead of jumping, and keeps its icon so it can be tapped shut again.

entries.title: Sort your follow lists
entries.detail: Followers and Following gain an A-Z switch beside the search field, and searching now reports how many people it is showing. AniList's own ordering stays the default.

entries.title: A demo that shows the whole profile
entries.detail: Demo mode's activity feed now includes a manga entry, so the type labels and the chapter wording can be reviewed alongside the anime rows - without an AniList account. The profile it opens already carried the four tabs, followers and statistics.

entries.title: Numbered lists in bios line up
entries.detail: An ordered list past its ninth item printed "10." wider than the bullet column and wrapped onto its own line, indenting every entry after it. The column now fits two digits.

entries.title: Anime Info & Specs Tab Repaired
entries.detail: Opening a sequel's detail sheet could fail to build the Anime Info & Specs tab, which referenced a specs grid the codebase no longer has. The tab now renders the current studio, schedule, rating and tag panels.

entries.title: Cover Art in the Detail Header
entries.detail: The detail header sat on a flat grey panel until AniList's wide banner arrived, and stayed that way for every entry that has no banner at all. It now falls back to the entry's own key visual and its dominant cover colour from the first frame.

entries.title: Instant Motion Is Actually Instant
entries.detail: The empty-state orb kept two invisible animation loops running behind a static shape in the Instant motion style. It no longer animates at all in that style.

entries.title: Smoother Empty-State Morphing
entries.detail: The orb's shape morph now animates in the draw phase, so it no longer recomposes the whole empty state on every frame it is on screen.

entries.title: Hold & Swipe to Currently Watching
entries.detail: Hold the quick add button with an animated progress fill and color transition to instantly add a sequel to Currently Watching, or perform a horizontal swipe gesture to add immediately.

entries.title: Quick Add Gestures in Settings
entries.detail: Configure button hold duration (3 seconds vs 5 seconds) and toggle the swipe gesture in Settings > Edit under Quick Add Gestures.

entries.title: Anime Info Tab Redesign
entries.detail: Completely modularized anime info tab with high-definition YouTube trailer cards, score distribution badges, rank achievements, production studio specs, and thematic tags.

entries.title: Material 3 Expressive Refinements
entries.detail: Polished spring physics, tactile haptic feedback on tab changes, and crisp pure-vector icons across the application.

entries.title: HD Cover Art & Interactive Artwork Viewer
entries.detail: Fetches extra-large high definition cover art directly from AniList with pinch-to-zoom up to 4x, double-tap zoom toggle, smooth panning, and dominant color ambient glow.

entries.title: Custom App Colors & Expanded Color Themes
entries.detail: Choose from new vibrant theme palettes (Cyber Jade, Neon Violet, Crimson, Deep Ocean) and pick any custom accent hue dynamically across the entire application.

entries.title: AniList Markdown Tables & Spoilers
entries.detail: Added complete Markdown table parsing and rendering with Material 3 container styling, enhanced spoiler block interactions, and inline formatting.

entries.title: Layout & Performance Optimizations
entries.detail: Improved poster tap ergonomics, refined profile tab clearances, and reduced unnecessary recompositions for silky smooth scrolling.

entries.title: Collapsible Currently Arriving Section
entries.detail: Easily expand or collapse the Currently Arriving anime carousel with an animated toggle button, smooth spring transitions, and persistent user preferences.

entries.title: Material 3 Expressive Morphing & Physics
entries.detail: Enhanced shape morphing in segmented controls, tabs, and navigation components with dynamic corner radius interpolation, fluid spring physics, and draw-phase transforms.

entries.title: UI & Animation Polish
entries.detail: Improved tactile touch targets, refined motion tokens across screens, and resolved layout bugs for a cleaner, more responsive experience.

entries.title: Complete AniList Markdown Engine
entries.detail: Full support for clickable linked images, HTML tags (underline, strikethrough, bold, italic), auto-detected web URLs, interactive spoilers, and checklists in user bios.

entries.title: Dashboard & Settings Refinements
entries.detail: Fixed filter state synchronization, enhanced theme card previews, and streamlined navigation clearances.

entries.title: Material 3 Expressive UI Polish
entries.detail: Spring transitions, enhanced touch targets, and responsive card layouts across all tabs.

entries.title: Improved list loading & caching
entries.detail: Enhanced AniList list synchronization with multi-chunk pagination support for large libraries, cross-referenced cache keys, and instant retrieval.

entries.title: AniList Markdown in profile
entries.detail: Rich formatting for user bios including interactive spoilers, clickable links, headers, code blocks, and blockquotes.

entries.title: Material 3 Expressive shapes
entries.detail: Refined geometric bounds scaling and aspect ratio preservation across custom shapes and morphing visual components.

entries.title: A complete profile experience
entries.detail: The Profile tab receives a full overhaul: banner artwork, an interactive 26-week activity heatmap calendar, expandable bios, and instant search through followers and following.

entries.title: Resilient profile loading
entries.detail: Public profiles and statistics stay accessible even when an account's list is private or unavailable, with automatic graceful fallback.

entries.title: Bug fixes & expressive polish
entries.detail: Fixed pagination triggers, social feed idle loading, and streamlined navigation bar clearances.

entries.title: Coming arrivals, your way
entries.detail: Settings > Edit gains a Dashboard card. Turn the Currently arriving rows off entirely, or compact them to plain no-poster rows that load nothing - less data, less battery, while you scan your list.

entries.title: Currently arriving
entries.detail: Your Watching and Planning lists get their own row above search: what is airing in front of you, with the next episode counted down, and what is announced with its start date. Airing first, soonest first.

entries.title: This year, only
entries.detail: Filters gains two switches: sequels that release this year, and sequels to shows you completed this year. Both live in the filter sheet and show what they are counting down from.

entries.title: Quicker public profiles
entries.detail: Opening someone else's profile no longer waits for one scan to finish before starting another. Settings copy now says what each field is for, and dead version checks are gone.

entries.title: Motion that matches you
entries.detail: Settings > Motion now offers Instant, Smooth or Chill. Chill is the full bouncy physics; Smooth is calm without overshoot; Instant skips motion entirely.

entries.title: A shape that turns, never snaps
entries.detail: The What's new orb morphs between Material shapes instead of sitting as a flat icon. The transition fades between lists and routes are gentler and resolved to a token.

entries.title: Android 12 and newer only
entries.detail: The app now requires Android 12 or newer. Every version check below that was dead code is gone.

entries.title: Your list refreshes itself
entries.detail: Pick how often the AniList list is re-read, in Settings > Edit. Default is 30 minutes.

entries.title: Release notes now match the build
entries.detail: What's new in the app and on the download page come from one file, so they cannot disagree.

entries.title: Release signing recovered
entries.detail: The signing key was rotated to a recoverable password. Builds from v1.0.17 to v1.0.22 cannot be updated over the top.

entries.title: Faster, steadier list loads
entries.detail: Optimised GraphQL batching and season mapping prevent connection failures.

entries.title: Planning syncs straight to AniList
entries.detail: Every addition lands on your account with instant confirmation.

entries.title: In-app updates
entries.detail: Checks GitHub releases and installs them in two taps.
